top5.why: Loops over rollupSize-derived tx count with raw assembly parsing and signature/approval handling for deposits and unchecked-return withdrawals.
Overwrites the proof-decoded numTxs with rollupSize, so the number of processed inner txs is not tied to the proven count.
Hand-built assembly staticcall to the verifier over mutated proofData memory; state is updated from unvalidated decoded values.
Calls permit on an arbitrary depositor with caller-chosen spender and amount, then credits deposits.
Ignores transferFrom return value and credits the full amount, so fee-on-transfer or false-returning tokens are over-credited.
Whitelist-skipped mint/burn of NFTs desyncs ERC20 balances from NFT holdings and can mint or burn at the supply bounds.
Mixed ERC20/ERC721 dispatch on valueOrId lets the id/amount ambiguity bypass checks and move NFT plus units without the normal mint/burn bookkeeping.
Mints new ids or reuses banked ids; whitelisting and the queue can exceed the 50 max supply or revert on transfers.
Banked NFTs are moved to the contract and queued, leaving ownership/queue state inconsistent with balances.
Cross-chain credit path mints ERC20 and NFTs, bounded only by per-chain totalSupply and whitelist state.
exitMarket has no pool-wide reentrancy guard, so it can be called from the ETH transfer callback in borrow before the borrow is recorded, releasing collateral.
doTransferOut sends the funds before accountBorrows and totalBorrows are written (checks-effects-interactions violated).
Raw call.value with full gas to the borrower hands control to an attacker contract mid-borrow.
Transfers out underlying before the redeemer's state is fully finalized, also allowing callback reentry.
Liquidity check relies on membership and balances that can be changed mid-borrow via reentrant exitMarket.
Single owner can replace any facet and run arbitrary delegatecall init code; governance-driven cuts bypass normal checks.
Delegatecalls arbitrary _init with arbitrary calldata in diamond storage context.
Applies Add/Replace/Remove cuts then runs init; any caller path reaching it can take over the diamond.
Reads the sender from trailing calldata when msg.sender is the diamond itself, enabling sender spoofing in owner checks.
Owner check relies on LibMeta.msgSender, which is spoofable when the diamond calls itself.
Signature does not bind msg.sender, swap aggregator, tokens or swap amounts (only data hashes), so a signed auth can be replayed or have its fields altered by anyone.
Approves and calls an unsigned, caller-supplied aggregator with arbitrary tokens/amounts from vault or strategy balances.
Executes caller-supplied swaps from the strategy, where fromToken can be the vault token and the aggregator is untrusted.
Share minting uses balance delta, with swap amounts and tokens not tied to auth.amount, and sender-based pulls.
Swap amounts out of vault balances are unsigned and not bounded by the withdrawn amount, so the vault's other balances can be drained.
Calls permit on the underlying and then pulls from an arbitrary 'from'; a token without real permit (e.g. WETH fallback) lets the call pass silently and steal from users who approved the router.
Same flaw: permit on a non-permit underlying silently succeeds, then transferFrom drains any approved 'from'.
Same unchecked permit then transferFrom(from) pattern.
Relies on transferWithPermit of an attacker-chosen token/underlying with arbitrary 'from'.
Relies on transferWithPermit of an attacker-chosen token/underlying with arbitrary 'from'.
Unrestricted, non-view delegatecall of arbitrary calldata into the handler in the proxy's storage context.
Unrestricted delegatecall of arbitrary calldata into the SI handler.
Liquidation lets liquidator and borrower overlap and updates storage without checking the caller or reward consistency.
Permissionless function that credits reserve and total deposits with transfer checks only on balance deltas.
Caller-supplied flag controls whether all handlers' interest is applied before computing collateralizable amounts.
Caller-controlled exchangeAddress and exchangeData are executed, so ERC20 transferFrom calldata on victims who approved the writer can be injected.
Low-level call to the attacker-supplied exchange with arbitrary data and all contract ETH, with no allow-list.
Accepts ETH from whatever address is set as exchange, which is attacker-controlled.
Pulls collateral from msg.sender with a caller-supplied acoToken and collateral address, so it trusts a fake ACO token.
Approves an arbitrary token/spender combination based on untrusted acoToken and erc20proxy interactions.
Upscales the requested amount and balances with mulDown and the tiny-amount rounding errors let the invariant be manipulated in the attacker's favour.
Uses mulDown for all amounts regardless of direction, so amounts in are under-counted.
Newton iteration plus +1 rounding on tiny amounts can return an amountIn below the true value.
BPT swaps upscale balances and amounts with rounding-down and update the invariant afterward, enabling accumulated rounding drift.
Iterative divUp/divDown mix and the invariant approximation lose precision at small balances.
